title: Python Advanced Concepts - Module #1455
question: Under what circumstance does the Python Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) release control to other threads?
options: Only when a thread runs for exactly 10,000 CPU instructions.
When the class `RequestHandler` invokes garbage collection.
During blocking I/O operations or explicit calls to time.sleep().
Never; Python is single-threaded and cannot run other threads.
answer: During blocking I/O operations or explicit calls to time.sleep().
explanation: The GIL is released during I/O operations, sleeping, or when C-extensions explicitly release it, allowing other threads to execute.
